Welcome to KR Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation Clinic

Physiotherapist · Physiotherapy at Home · Physiotherapy Clinic in Noida

Physiotherapy — more popularly known as medical therapy — helps patients rehabilitate from disease, injury, disability and chronic pain. Our physiotherapists have a deep understanding of how the body works and help patients recover from pain, injury, paralysis, ligament injury and neurological conditions, treating both chronic pain and acute problems.

Best Physiotherapy Service in Noida

KR Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation Clinic provides the best physiotherapy service in Noida. Our physiotherapists are highly qualified, and the clinic focuses on maintaining health for people of all ages — helping patients manage pain and prevent disease.

This treatment is very effective, but only when the practising physiotherapist has proper experience. The therapist must know how to assess and how to treat. A physiotherapist knows very well how each body part works — and if a body part stops working, they know how to restore it. That is why proper assessment, knowledge and experience matter so much.

Led by Dr. Neelam Sharma(PT) & Team

Dr. Neelam Sharma(PT) and her team work for the welfare of patients suffering from orthopaedic problems, chronic pain conditions, sports injuries, neurological problems, women’s health issues and geriatric conditions.

Our effort is to treat patients without surgery — therapy that acts like medicine, yet is cheaper, safer and more beneficial than drugs, with no side effects.

If a loved one at home is suffering from a condition that limits their life, contact the best physiotherapist in Noida — KR Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation Clinic.

title: Privacy Policy
subtitle: Last updated: 5 October 2026
content_html:
Last updated: 5 October 2026. This Privacy Policy explains how KR Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation Clinic (“we”, “us”, “our”, “the Clinic”) collects, uses, discloses and protects your personal information when you visit https://www.krphysiotherapy.com, book an appointment, call or message us, or receive treatment at the clinic or at your home.

We are committed to handling your personal data responsibly and in accordance with applicable Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“DPDP Act”), and professional confidentiality obligations that apply to healthcare providers.

1. Information We Collect

  • Identity and contact details — your name, phone number, email address and residential address, when you book an appointment, submit an enquiry form, or contact us by phone, WhatsApp or email.
  • Appointment details — the service you request, your preferred date and time, and any notes you choose to share about your condition.
  • Health information — symptoms, medical history, previous treatments, prescriptions, investigation reports and other clinical information that you or your referring doctor provide to us for assessment and treatment.
  • Payment information — records of fees charged and payments received. We do not store your card or banking credentials.
  • Technical information — IP address, browser and device type, pages visited and referring website, collected through server logs and analytics when you browse our website.

2. How We Use Your Information

  • To schedule, confirm, remind and manage your appointments (including by phone, SMS, WhatsApp or email).
  • To assess your condition, provide physiotherapy treatment and maintain clinical records.
  • To respond to your enquiries and provide information about our services.
  • To process fees and maintain basic accounts and billing records.
  • To improve our website, services and patient experience.
  • To comply with legal, regulatory and professional obligations applicable to a healthcare practice.
  • Only with your consent — to send you occasional health tips, clinic updates or offers. You can opt out at any time.

We do not use your personal data for any purpose that is incompatible with the purposes set out above without informing you.

3. Health and Sensitive Personal Data

Information about your health is treated as sensitive personal data. We handle it with a higher standard of care, limit access to the physiotherapist and staff directly involved in your care or the administration of your appointments, and never sell it or use it for unrelated commercial purposes. We disclose health information only:

  • to the treating physiotherapist and clinic staff involved in your care;
  • to a referring or receiving doctor, where you ask us to share it or it is necessary for your treatment;
  • with your consent;
  • where disclosure is required by law, court order, or a competent regulatory authority.

4. Consent and Legal Basis

Where we process your personal data based on consent (for example, when you submit an appointment form or share health information), that consent is freely given, specific and informed, and you may withdraw it at any time by contacting us. Withdrawing consent may mean we are unable to continue providing treatment or related services. We may also process limited personal data where necessary to comply with a legal obligation, or to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim.

5. Sharing and Disclosure

We do not sell, rent or trade your personal information. We share it only with:

  • Service providers that help us operate — for example website hosting, appointment and communication tools (such as WhatsApp), mapping and analytics services — under confidentiality obligations and only to the extent needed to perform their function.
  • Treating clinicians, as described above.
  • Authorities, where disclosure is required by law or to protect the safety, rights or property of our patients, staff or the public.

6. Data Retention

We keep your personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy and for the retention of clinical records required under applicable healthcare regulations. Records that are no longer required are securely deleted or de-identified.

7. Data Security

We apply reasonable technical and organisational safeguards appropriate to a clinical practice — including restricted access to records and encrypted transport for data submitted through our website. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security, but we take the protection of your data seriously and review our practices regularly.

8. Cookies and Analytics

Our website uses essential cookies and basic analytics to understand how visitors use the site and to improve it. You can control or delete cookies through your browser settings; doing so may affect some website functionality.

9. Third-Party Links and Embeds

Our website may embed or link to third-party services such as Google Maps, WhatsApp, and our social media pages (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn). These services are governed by their own privacy policies, and we encourage you to review them. We are not responsible for the privacy practices of third-party websites.

10. Children’s Privacy

We provide physiotherapy to children only with the knowledge and consent of a parent or legal guardian, who should accompany minor patients and provide the information we need for treatment. We do not knowingly collect personal data directly from children without such parental involvement.

11. Your Rights

Subject to applicable law, you have the right to:

  • access the personal data we hold about you and know how it is processed;
  • request correction, completion or updating of inaccurate or incomplete data;
  • request erasure of your data where retention is no longer legally required;
  • withdraw consent for optional processing (such as marketing messages);
  • raise a grievance about how your data has been handled.

To exercise any of these rights, contact our Grievance Officer using the details below. We will respond within a reasonable period, normally within 30 days.

12. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. The “Last updated” date at the top of this page shows the current version. Material changes will be highlighted on our website.

13. Contact Us / Grievance Officer

For any questions, requests or grievances regarding this Privacy Policy or your personal data, please contact:

content_html:
Physiotherapy - Types, Treatment and Procedure

With the help of physiotherapy one can restore mobility and normalcy in their life after affected by an injury, disease or disability. A physiotherapy session includes manual therapy, advising and educating the patient. It is helpful for patient of any age to manage further pain and prevent subsequent injuries or diseases.

Physiotherapy clinics in Noida sector 34 adopt a more holistic approach to a patient's treatment process by taking into consideration their lifestyle and other dimensions.

Types Of Physiotherapy Treatments

  • Neurological: It is given when there is a loss of balance and coordination, weakness of the muscles, loss of function, muscle spasms, and decrease in sensation. The aim is to establish mobility of the body part and to treat the functional disorders.
  • Orthopedic: The aim of this is to treat diseases related to the musculoskeletal system, including correcting the muscles, bones, ligaments, joints, and tendons.
  • Post-Surgical Rehabilitation: This therapy is given to patients recovering after an operation. The main aim is to restore strength, mobility and confidence through progressive, guided exercise.
  • Pediatric: It is done to improve the acute injuries found in children in the time of birth involving certain genetic defects or delay in physical growth.
  • Geriatric: In this, age-related matters are treated such as osteoporosis and arthritis.
  • Vestibular rehabilitation: The main focus of this is to bring back the balance of the body which is caused by a problem in the inner ear.

How Is Physiotherapy Done?

Best physiotherapists in sector 34 Noida uses a variety of techniques, resolute by the nature of the injury sustained and particular problem that is being treated. The common one of them is:

  • Manual manipulation: Moving the soft tissues and the joints better circulation flushes excess fluids from the body.
  • Electrical stimulation of the nerves: Delivering electric currents in controlled intensity helps to contain the pain signals.
  • Acupuncture: This is a great way of stimulating the CNS.
  • Demonstration: Demonstrating proper movement patterns help patients to recover on their own.

Who needs physiotherapy?

Persons suffering from following conditions:

  • Injured while playing
  • Suffering with chronic pain
  • During and after pregnancy
  • During and after surgery
  • Recover comfortably during and after pregnancy
  • Prevent from thrombosis
  • Prevent from pressure sores
  • Prevent muscle wasting and joint mobility

title: Physiotherapy in Noida Sector 35
subtitle: Best Physiotherapy Clinic & Home Care in Noida Sector 35
content_html:
Techniques of Physiotherapy

Physiotherapy uses different treatments and applies preventative approaches as per the specific problems you are experiencing.

First visit is for assessment to help determine what help you might need. The main approaches physiotherapists in sector 35 Noida may use are:

  • Education and advice
  • Movement and exercise
  • Manual therapy

Sometimes other techniques may also be tried.

Education and Advice

The main aspect of physiotherapy is looking at the body as a whole and not focusing on the individual factors of an injury.

Thus, providing general advice about ways to improve wellbeing – such as, by taking regular exercise and maintaining a healthy weight– is an important part of treatment.

A physiotherapist also gives specific advice for everyday activities and reduces risk of pain or injury.For example, for back pain, you may be given advice about good posture, lifting or carrying techniques, and avoiding twisting, over-stretching or prolonged standing.

Movement and Exercise

Physiotherapists usually recommend movement and exercise for improving your mobility and function. This may include:

  • Exercises to improve movement and strength– these need to be repeated regularly for a set length of time.
  • Activities involving moving whole body, such as walking or swimming for recovering from an operation or injury.
  • Exercises carried out in warm, shallow water; the water help relax and support the muscles and joints.
  • Advice and exercises to help you increase or maintain your physical activity.
  • Providing mobility aids

Manual Therapy

Manual therapy is a technique where a physiotherapist uses their hands for manipulating, mobilizing and massaging the body tissues for:

  • Relieving pain and stiffness
  • Improving blood circulation
  • Helping fluid drain more efficiently from body parts
  • Improving the movement of different body parts
  • Promoting relaxation

Manual therapy treats specific problems, such as back pain and a range of conditions that don't affect the bones, joints or muscles.

Other Techniques

Other techniques used by best physiotherapy clinics in Noida sector 35 to help ease pain and promote healing include:

  • Acupuncture – where fine needles are inserted into specific points, with the aim of reducing pain
  • Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) – A small, battery-operated device is used to deliver an electric current for relieving pain
  • Ultrasound – Where high-frequency sound waves are used to treat deep tissue injuries

Some people have found these treatments effective, but there isn't much scientific evidence.

title: Physiotherapy in Noida Sector 52
subtitle: Best Physiotherapy Clinic & Home Care in Noida Sector 52
content_html:
Physiotherapist in a Rehabilitation Team

Physiotherapy is governed internationally by World Physiotherapy, this shows that the profession is responsible for achieving the profession’s scope of practice and defining the roles of physiotherapists in sector 52 Noida, with National Physiotherapy Associations. Physiotherapy is an autonomous profession and it can be operated as members of health service provider or rehabilitation teams or as independent practitioners.

Where Physiotherapists Work

Physiotherapists work in a wide range of public, private and voluntary sector settings;

  • Hospitals: In outpatients, on medical and surgical wards and in specialized units;
  • Community and Primary Care Health Centers: In health centers or visiting people in their homes, assessing and treating a wide variety of muscle, joint and ligament problems and women’s health, neurological and orthopaedic conditions and many more;
  • Schools: Helping children achieve their full potential;
  • Workplace: Providing assessments, pre-employment screening, risk management and educating workers in correct techniques;
  • Private Practice: Assessing and treating a wide variety of muscle, joint and ligament problems and many more.

Knowledge and Skills

After professional training, best physiotherapy clinics in Noida sector 52 should have the knowledge, skills and judgment to provide services for musculoskeletal and orthopedic function, neurological, muscular, skeletal, postural and vestibular function, and prescription of assistive devices to optimize function.

Physiotherapists use their professional knowledge and practical skills, together with thinking skills and skills for interaction to identify what is limiting an individual’s movement.

Assessment and Identification

The examination with actual or potential impairments, activity limitations, or participation restrictions by using specific tests and measures. Physiotherapists are required to:

  • Undertake a comprehensive assessment of the patient
  • Evaluate the findings from the assessment to make clinical judgments
  • Implement a physical therapist treatment program and education in agreement
  • Evaluate and re-evaluate the outcomes of any treatments
  • Make recommendations for self-management
  • Collaborate with health professionals and other key stakeholders
  • Formulate a diagnosis
  • Provide consultation within their expertise

Intervention and Treatment

Intervention and treatment is aimed to prevent impairments, activity limitations, participatory restrictions, disability and injury. The physiotherapist determines the interventions and manages the needs of the individual as per the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, plan, goals and outcomes of the planned interventions. Intervention is implemented and modified to reach agreed goals and interventions may include:

  • Education
  • Therapeutic Exercise
  • Functional training
  • Manual therapy techniques
  • Prescription, application, and fabrication of devices/equipment
  • Electrotherapeutic modalities
  • Physical agents and mechanical modalities

title: Physiotherapy in Noida Sector 71
subtitle: Best Physiotherapy Clinic & Home Care in Noida Sector 71
content_html:
What Physiotherapists do?

Physiotherapy involves the treatment of injury, disease and disorders through any physical methods — such as exercise, massage, manipulation and other treatments.

Becoming a physiotherapist can be incredibly rewarding; in your daily work, you would be helping people who have been injured to recover from and come back to their normal conditions and live more independently. Best physiotherapy clinics in Noida sector 71 treats patients across a wide age range – from young children to the elderly.

Most of the people believe that physiotherapists work mainly with back and sports-related injuries, but that’s not true. Physiotherapists are highly trained professionals who do provide treatment for those suffering from physical problems that can be caused due to injury, disease, illness and ageing.

The main purpose of physiotherapist is to improve a person's quality of life with the use of variety of treatments to alleviate pain and restore function or, lessen the effects of any dysfunction.

Career Development Opportunities

There are several opportunities to advance your career and many career pathways in the public health system. Some private practitioners expand their practices to offer additional services, such as Pilates classes.

Physiotherapy doctor in sector-71 Noida can complete a course to become a credentialed diabetes educator, and there is also the future possibility that they can prescribe some medications for pain and mobility-related conditions, however, this may take a number of years. It can also happen that critical care physiotherapists will be using techniques such as ultrasound in the future.

Role Of The Physiotherapist

The role is varied and rarely is the same. A physiotherapist may assess the physical condition of a patient to diagnose problems and offer a treatment plan, or they can also be re-training patients to walk, or cope with crutches, walking frames, or wheelchairs.

Physiotherapists spend much time educating patients to prevent further injuries and to help people lead a healthy lifestyle.

Physiotherapists in sector 71 Noida may also plan and implement community fitness programs. Finally, they can also issue sick leave certificates.

During their career, they treat all manner of people including children, premature babies, pregnant women, people undergoing rehabilitation, athletes, the elderly, and those need help following injuries, strokes, or major surgery.

Key Duties Of A Physiotherapist

Physiotherapists use a variety of techniques for those who are affected by injuries caused by illness, disability or ageing.

Some of the responsibilities include:

  • Diagnosing and treating various physical problems
  • Developing treatment programs
  • Conducting therapeutic exercise sessions
  • Using specialist techniques
  • Collecting and analyzing data
  • Writing reports and case notes
  • Liaising with other health professionals
  • Educating and training patients
  • Keeping up to date with the latest industry knowledge

Most patients need between six and twelve sessions depending on the condition, though severe or long-standing problems take longer. You will always know what the next step is before you leave.

Treatment Available In-Clinic

  • Electrotherapy including TENS, interferential therapy and therapeutic ultrasound
